name: Sheraton Grand London Park Lane
positioning: A Grade II listed hotel that debuted in the 1920s and overlooks Green Park, with the Art Deco Palm Court, Art Deco suites and rooms with Green Park views, a short stroll from Buckingham Palace and Westminster
best_for: City-break travelers who want to walk to Buckingham Palace and Westminster
Lovers of Art Deco design and historic listed buildings
Families who would enjoy a London-themed kids' afternoon tea

facts.text: Buckingham Palace and Westminster are a short stroll from the hotel.
Green Park Underground Station is a 5-minute walk from the hotel.
The hotel made its debut in the 1920s.
Guests can reserve rooms with views of Green Park.
Rooms have bathrobes, slippers and spacious wet rooms with Sheraton-branded toiletries.
The suites have Art Deco interiors.
Club Rooms are on the higher levels of the hotel.
All Club Rooms and Suites include access to the Club Lounge.
The Sheraton Club Lounge serves a hot buffet breakfast plus beverages, snacks and canapes throughout the day.
The concierge team are members of Les Clefs d'Or.
The London Kids' Afternoon Tea includes playful pastries of the London Eye, a London red bus and Big Ben.

highlights.text: The entire hotel is a Grade II listed building, notably the Silver Gallery, the Ballroom, the Oak Room and the Palm Court.
The Grand Park View Suite has a view of the Royal Parks.
The Palm Court keeps its 1920s Art Deco details, including a stained-glass ceiling, a marble floor and the original bar.
The hotel's Pawsome Staycation for dogs includes a dog bed, bowls, a complimentary dogtail in the Smith & Whistle bar and an in-room dog's day out in London itinerary.

considerations.text: There is no on-site parking; discounted parking is available nearby.
Rooms do not have a fridge.
WhataHotel notes the busy central London location brings high foot traffic in the surrounding area.
